faq.q: Is October a good month for a boat charter in Estepona?
faq.a: Yes. October is shoulder season: the summer crowds are gone, the sea is still warm (21°C), and the air stays around 24°C. You get calm conditions, clear skies, and fewer boats at anchor. It's ideal for a relaxed day out, coastal cruising, or even a light-water swim.

faq.q: What is the weather like in Estepona in October?
faq.a: Expect daytime highs of 24°C, dropping to 17°C at night. The Mediterranean water is 21°C—still swimmable for most. Sunshine averages 8 hours per day, with a 20% chance of a brief shower. Winds are light (8-12 knots), so sea conditions are usually calm.

faq.q: Do I need a wetsuit for swimming in October?
faq.a: Not necessarily. At 21°C, the water is brisk but tolerable for a 10-15 minute swim. If you're sensitive to cold, a thin shorty wetsuit adds comfort. Many guests just bring a towel and jump in—especially in the shallow coves near Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés.

faq.q: Which boats are available for an October charter?
faq.a: Our entire fleet is available from Puerto Banús. For a small group, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) work well. For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) includes a free jet ski. All include a skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks.

faq.q: How far is Estepona from Puerto Banús by boat?
faq.a: Estepona is about 15 nautical miles west of Puerto Banús. At a cruising speed of 20-25 knots, it takes roughly 40-50 minutes. Most charters combine a run along the coast with stops at Cabopino, Cala del Faro, or straight to Estepona's marina for lunch.

faq.q: What should I wear for an October boat trip?
faq.a: Layers are key. Start with a light jumper or windbreaker over a t-shirt; it's cooler at sea. Bring sunglasses, sunscreen (SPF 30+), and a hat. In the afternoon sun, you'll be comfortable in shorts. A light waterproof jacket is wise if a shower is forecast.

faq.q: Can we still anchor and swim in October?
faq.a: Absolutely. The sea is calm, and the water is 21°C—swimmable. Popular anchor spots like Cala Cortés and the area off Estepona's coast are quieter than in July. Your skipper will choose a sheltered spot based on the day's wind and swell.

faq.q: How do I book a boat for October from Estepona?
faq.a: You can book via WhatsApp—our team responds within the hour. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), rates are €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, all inclusive. For larger yachts like the Mangusta 80, pricing is on request. October slots fill fast, so book early.

data.body_html:
October in Estepona is a hidden gem for boaters: the summer heat fades, but the Mediterranean stays warm at 21°C, and the sea is often glassy calm. With 8 hours of daily sunshine and air temperatures peaking at 24°C, it's the perfect shoulder-season window for a leisurely charter along the Costa del Sol. Our fleet, departing from Puerto Banús, is fully equipped with licensed skippers, fuel, drinks, and snacks—so you can focus on the views.

Why October Works for an Estepona Boat Charter

October avoids the two extremes: the crowded, hot summer and the cooler, windier winter. The sea temperature stays at a comfortable 21°C—still warm enough for a dip—and the typical wind is just 8-12 knots from the east, keeping the swell below 0.5m. You'll have the anchorages near Estepona, Cala del Faro, and Cala Cortés largely to yourself, with clear visibility for spotting dolphins along the coast.

Estepona Boat Charter Weather October: What to Expect

These conditions are ideal for a stable, comfortable ride. The mornings are crisp, the afternoons warm, and the light is golden—perfect for photography off the Golden Mile.

Best Boats for an October Charter

Depending on your group size, we have options from Puerto Banús:

  • Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) – agile and economical for a small crew.
  • Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) – a sporty bowrider for a quick coastal blast.
  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) – Tier A at €749 for 2h or €2,299 for 8h, all inclusive.
  • Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) – same Tier A pricing, a touch more space.
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – flagship option, min 4h at €4,719 with a free jet ski.

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT. For other boats, message us on WhatsApp for a tailored quote.

Sample October Itinerary: Puerto Banús to Estepona

Depart Puerto Banús at 10:00. Cruise west at 20 knots, passing Marbella Marina and the green slopes of La Concha. By 10:45 you're off the coast of Estepona—drop anchor at Cala Cortés for a swim in the 21°C water. Lunch at a chiringuito near Estepona's marina, then a slow cruise back, stopping at Cala del Faro for a final dip. Return by 16:00, with time to enjoy the golden afternoon light.

What's Included in Your October Charter

No hidden extras. Every booking includes:

  • Licensed, English-speaking skipper
  • Fuel for the full trip
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks (olives, crisps, fruit)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

Bring your own food if you like—there's a cooler on board. The skipper will also tailor the route to the day's weather.

October Events and Local Colour

October is harvest season in the region. After your charter, stop at a bodega near Estepona for a wine tasting, or walk the old town's flower-filled streets. The marina at Estepona is quieter than in summer, so you can moor easily and enjoy a fresh seafood lunch. If you're staying in Marbella, the Golden Mile's beach clubs are still open, though with a more relaxed vibe.

Booking Tips for October

October weather is generally stable, but a cool front can bring a morning shower—your skipper will adjust the route if needed. Book at least 48 hours ahead via WhatsApp to secure your preferred boat. For Tier A boats, the 8-hour rate (€2,299) is the best value if you want a full day. For the Mangusta 80, the 4-hour minimum (€4,719) includes a jet ski—perfect for exploring the coast at speed.
